stories.title: X replaces creator revenue-sharing with 'Original Content Rewards'
stories.summary: X is discontinuing its ad revenue-sharing program for creators and replacing it with a new system called Original Content Rewards, according to The Verge and TechCrunch. TechCrunch reports X described the old program as 'misaligned,' suggesting the new system aims to tie payouts more directly to original content rather than engagement-based ad splits. Neither report detailed the exact mechanics of how rewards will be calculated.
stories.whyItMatters: Creator payment structures shape what content gets made on one of the largest social platforms, and changes here could push other platforms to rethink how they compensate creators.
whatToWatch: Rollout timeline and eligibility details for Original Content Rewards
Creator reaction to whether payouts rise or fall under the new system
questions: What specific metrics determine rewards under the new program?
Does this reduce incentives for engagement-bait content that thrived under ad revenue sharing?

Specific location, capacity, and emissions figures weren't detailed in the report.

stories.summary: Wired reports on a proposal that would change how the US Census collects data, reportedly ending counts of undocumented immigrants and dropping questions on race and sexual orientation. stories.title: Trump administration has now spent nearly $4B to cancel offshore wind projects
stories.summary: The Trump administration has spent close to $4 billion canceling offshore wind farm projects, including a recently reported additional $1.2 billion, according to Engadget and TechCrunch. Ars Technica frames the broader campaign against wind power as increasingly costly and, in its analysis, not proceeding as the administration intended. The moves are part of a wider rollback of renewable energy projects.
stories.whyItMatters: Energy policy shifts affect the power mix available to tech companies, including increasingly power-hungry AI data centers, and add regulatory uncertainty for renewable energy investment.
whatToWatch: Further project cancellations or legal challenges from developers
Total taxpayer cost as the campaign continues
questions: What legal authority is being used to cancel already-approved projects?
